statement: Whenever spiral_matrix m n head returns a result r, r is exactly the m by n matrix defined as follows. len(r) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(r[i]) = n, with rows indexed 0..m-1 and columns indexed 0..n-1. Let the clockwise spiral order of an m by n matrix be the sequence of all m*n cells obtained by repeatedly traversing the current outer boundary of the not-yet-visited cells: left-to-right along the top row, top-to-bottom along the right column, right-to-left along the bottom row, and bottom-to-top along the left column, then moving inward; if only one row or one column remains, it is traversed in the only direction that continues the spiral. For every k with 0 <= k < m*n, if (i,j) is the k-th cell in this clockwise spiral order (0-indexed), then r[i][j] is the value of the k-th node of head if k < L, and r[i][j] = -1 if k >= L.
preconditions: Let L be the number of nodes (Cons cells) in head. The inputs satisfy the problem constraints: m and n are integers with 1 <= m, 1 <= n, and m*n <= 100000; 1 <= L <= m*n; and every node value v of head satisfies 0 <= v <= 1000.

statement: For every m, n, and head satisfying the preconditions, spiral_matrix m n head returns a result r; it does not panic, fail an overflow check, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: Let L be the number of nodes (Cons cells) in head. The inputs satisfy the problem constraints: m and n are integers with 1 <= m, 1 <= n, and m*n <= 100000; 1 <= L <= m*n; and every node value v of head satisfies 0 <= v <= 1000.
